subject: Mental Models
title: The Compound Effect of Models
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Compound Effect of Models.

hook.text: Warren Buffett credits reading as his superpower. He says knowledge compounds like interest over decades.

buildup.text: One mental model is useful. Ten models start connecting to each other and revealing hidden patterns.

discovery.text: At a certain point, new models snap into your existing web instantly. Learning accelerates the more you know.

twist.text: This is why early learning feels slow and later learning feels fast. The network effect kicks in.

climax.text: Buffett and Munger built their fortunes not on stock tips but on accumulated mental models from every field.

punchline.text: Models compound. The hundredth model is worth more than the first.

quiz.question: Why does learning new mental models get easier over time?
options: New models connect to your existing network, creating compound returns
